## CL-OA-002 — OASIS Quality Review & Error Correction
### 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-OA-002 |
| Policy Title | OASIS Quality Review & Error Correction |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | OA — OASIS & Assessment Governance |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

### 2. Purpose
This policy establishes a structured, multi-layered quality review process for completed OASIS assessments and defines the error correction and resubmission process at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. OASIS quality review is the clinical governance mechanism that stands between an assessor's work product and the consequences that OASIS data produces — PDGM payment classification, quality measure calculation, public reporting, and survey documentation. Without a rigorous quality review layer, individual assessor errors propagate unchecked into payment distortions, quality measure inaccuracies, and billing compliance vulnerabilities.
The OASIS quality review program serves two distinct functions that are equally essential. The pre-submission quality review — conducted before the OASIS is locked and transmitted — is the opportunity to correct errors before they create consequences. An error caught at pre-submission is simply corrected; it costs time but produces no regulatory, financial, or billing harm. The post-submission audit — conducted on a sample basis after transmission — is the quality assurance mechanism that identifies systemic patterns in OASIS accuracy, drives targeted training, validates that the pre-submission review is effective, and generates the data the QAPI program needs to measure clinical assessment quality over time.
A robust error correction process is equally critical. Errors will occur — the OASIS is a complex, multi-item instrument requiring clinical judgment, and human error is inevitable. The question is not whether errors will be made, but whether the agency has a process for identifying them and correcting them promptly, accurately, and in compliance with CMS correction methodology requirements. This policy establishes both layers — review and correction — with the specificity and accountability required to make them operationally effective.
### 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All authorized RN assessors who conduct comprehensive OASIS assessments
The designated OASIS Quality Reviewer (a role defined in Section 5 and CL-CA-002) — typically the Director of Nursing or a clinician with advanced OASIS training designated by the Director of Nursing
The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager who oversees the quality review program
The OASIS Transmission Coordinator who processes corrections
The Compliance Officer who is notified of systemic accuracy failures and payment-affecting corrections
Revenue Cycle staff who must hold claims pending correction of identified errors
### 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Every OASIS assessment submitted by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall undergo a structured quality review process before submission to the CMS repository. The pre-submission quality review is not optional for any assessor and is not waivable for any time point.
4.2 The agency shall designate a qualified OASIS Quality Reviewer who holds current, advanced OASIS competency and is authorized to conduct independent clinical review of OASIS assessments. The OASIS Quality Reviewer shall not be the same individual as the assessing RN for the assessment under review.
4.3 The quality review process shall operate at three levels: (a) Level 1 — Self-Review: the assessing RN completes the Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist per CL-OA-019 before locking every assessment; (b) Level 2 — OASIS Quality Reviewer Review: the designated Quality Reviewer independently reviews all SOC assessments within 5 business days of locking; quarterly random samples of all other time point assessments; (c) Level 3 — Director of Nursing Monthly Audit: the Director of Nursing conducts a monthly audit of ≥5% of all locked assessments from the prior month per CL-CA-002.
4.4 When the Level 1, Level 2, or Level 3 review identifies an error in a locked assessment — whether before or after submission — the error shall be corrected using the CMS-compliant correction process defined in Section 6.4. The correction shall be clinically justified and documented before processing. No correction shall be made for any reason other than to improve the accuracy of the assessment relative to the patient's actual clinical status at the time of the original assessment.
4.5 The prohibition on financially motivated corrections is absolute: OASIS corrections shall not be initiated for the purpose of increasing or decreasing the patient's PDGM payment group, improving quality measure scores, or any other financial or administrative purpose. Every correction must be clinically justified in writing. The Compliance Officer shall review all corrections that result in a change to the patient's PDGM payment group.
4.6 The agency's target OASIS data accuracy rate — defined as the percentage of audited items where the agency's response correctly reflects the CMS guidance for the patient's clinical status — is ≥95% across all item categories. An accuracy rate below 95% in any item category in any quarter shall trigger a targeted Performance Improvement Project per QA-PI-001.
4.7 Individual RN assessor accuracy rates shall be tracked and reported to the Director of Nursing monthly. Assessors with item category accuracy rates below 85% shall receive targeted retraining within 14 calendar days of the finding.
### 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| OASIS Quality Reviewer | A designated registered nurse with advanced OASIS competency who independently reviews completed OASIS assessments for accuracy, consistency, and compliance with CMS guidance. Must be different from the assessing RN for each reviewed assessment. |
| Pre-Submission Quality Review | The Level 1 self-review conducted by the assessing RN using the Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist (CL-OA-019) before locking every assessment. Required for every assessment at every time point. |
| Level 2 Review | The independent post-lock review conducted by the OASIS Quality Reviewer — for all SOC assessments within 5 business days, and quarterly random samples of other time points. |
| Level 3 Review | The Director of Nursing's monthly audit of ≥5% of all locked assessments from the prior month, per CL-CA-002. |
| Error | An OASIS item response that does not accurately reflect the patient's clinical status at the time of the assessment as it should be coded per the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual. |
| Correction | The process of inactivating an incorrect OASIS response and replacing it with the accurate response through the CMS-approved correction methodology, with clinical justification documented before processing. |
| Inactivation | The CMS process of voiding an OASIS record from the repository entirely — used when a record should not have been submitted (e.g., patient was not actually admitted, wrong time point was used). Distinguished from a correction, which replaces specific item responses. |
| OASIS Accuracy Rate | The percentage of audited OASIS item responses that correctly reflect the CMS guidance for the patient's clinical status, as determined by independent expert review. Calculated by item category and overall. |
| Financially Motivated Correction | A correction initiated for the purpose of changing the patient's PDGM payment group, improving quality measure scores, or any purpose other than clinical accuracy — explicitly prohibited by this policy and by CMS guidance. |

### 6. Procedures
#### 6.1 Level 1 Review — Assessing RN Self-Review

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Assessing RN | Before locking any OASIS assessment, complete the Pre-Submission Quality Review Checklist per CL-OA-019. The checklist systematically verifies: all applicable time point items are completed; no items are at default values without clinical justification; internal consistency is verified across related item groups (functional items, wound items, behavioral health items, medication items, clinical severity items); narrative documentation supports all OASIS responses; homebound status documentation meets the standards of CL-CA-005; and skilled service need documentation is present per CL-CA-001. | Before locking every OASIS assessment. |
| 6.1.2 | Assessing RN | If the self-review identifies any item that is not supported by documentation, any internal inconsistency, or any response the assessor is uncertain about, do not lock the assessment. Review the clinical record to resolve the issue, consult the Director of Nursing or OASIS Quality Reviewer if needed, and correct the response before locking. Document the self-review completion in the EHR per CL-OA-019. | Before locking. |
| 6.1.3 | Assessing RN | If any item requires clinical consultation to determine the correct response, contact the Director of Nursing or OASIS Quality Reviewer before locking. Document the consultation, the guidance received, and the final coding decision with the clinical rationale per CL-OA-012. | Before locking. |

#### 6.2 Level 2 Review — OASIS Quality Reviewer Independent Review

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | Review all SOC assessments within 5 business days of locking, using the OASIS Quality Review Tool per CL-CA-002 (Appendix A of CL-CA-002). The review shall assess each high-risk item category independently: GG functional items; wound items (M1311–M1350); behavioral health items (M1700–M1750); medication management items (M2001–M2010); clinical severity items; and homebound/skilled need documentation. | Within 5 business days of SOC assessment locking. |
| 6.2.2 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | Conduct quarterly random sample reviews of ROC, RECERT, FU, TRN, and DC assessments, reviewing a minimum of 10% of each time point from the prior quarter, using the same Quality Review Tool. | Quarterly; within 15 calendar days of quarter end. |
| 6.2.3 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | For each reviewed assessment, document findings in the OASIS Quality Review Log per CL-CA-002 (Appendix B of CL-CA-002): the assessment date, assessing RN, items reviewed, Reviewer determination (Accurate / Inaccurate / Insufficient Documentation), and any correction recommended. | At the time of each review. |
| 6.2.4 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | If an inaccuracy is identified: (a) document the specific item, the submitted response, the Reviewer's determination of the correct response, and the clinical evidence supporting the correction; (b) notify the assessing RN and the Director of Nursing within 24 hours; (c) if the assessment has already been transmitted to CMS, initiate the correction process per Section 6.4. | Within 24 hours of finding. |
| 6.2.5 | OASIS Quality Reviewer | When the assessing RN and the Quality Reviewer disagree on the correct response: the disagreement shall be escalated to the Director of Nursing for clinical adjudication within 24 hours. The Director of Nursing's determination is the agency's official coding position for that item. If the Director of Nursing agrees with the Quality Reviewer's finding and the assessment has already been submitted, initiate the correction process. Document the adjudication. | Escalation within 24 hours of disagreement. |

#### 6.3 Level 3 Review — Director of Nursing Monthly Audit

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Director of Nursing | Conduct a monthly OASIS accuracy audit of a random sample of ≥5% of all locked assessments from the prior month, per CL-CA-002. The audit shall include all time points proportionally — not exclusively SOC assessments. | Monthly. |
| 6.3.2 | Director of Nursing | Calculate monthly OASIS accuracy rates by item category and by individual assessor per CL-CA-002 (Appendix C of CL-CA-002 — OASIS Accuracy Dashboard). | Within 5 business days of audit completion. |
| 6.3.3 | Director of Nursing | Provide individual written feedback to each audited assessor within 14 calendar days, including: specific items where errors were identified; the submitted response; the correct response; the clinical evidence and CMS guidance supporting the correction; and the pattern of accuracy across the audited period. | Within 14 calendar days of audit completion. |
| 6.3.4 | Director of Nursing | For any assessor with an item category accuracy rate below 85%, initiate targeted retraining within 14 calendar days and conduct a follow-up audit of that assessor's next 5 completed assessments. Document all retraining and follow-up activities in the personnel file. | Within 14 calendar days of identifying below-standard performance. |
| 6.3.5 | Director of Nursing | Present aggregate monthly accuracy data to the QAPI Committee quarterly. Identify systemic patterns requiring program-level intervention. | Quarterly QAPI meeting. |

#### 6.4 Error Correction Process — Pre-Submission and Post-Submission

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Director of Nursing / OASIS Quality Reviewer | When an error is identified in any OASIS assessment — whether before or after submission — complete the Correction Assessment Form (Appendix A of this policy) before initiating any correction. The form shall document: the specific item in error; the submitted response; the correct response; the clinical evidence in the medical record supporting the correct response; the reason the original response was inaccurate; and whether the correction results in a PDGM payment group change. | Before initiating any correction. |
| 6.4.2 | Director of Nursing | Review and approve the Correction Assessment Form before any correction is processed. The Director of Nursing's review confirms: the correction is clinically justified by documented clinical evidence; the correction reflects the patient's actual status at the time of the original assessment — not a subsequent change in status; and the correction is not being made for financial or administrative reasons. Sign and date the form. | Before correction processing. |
| 6.4.3 | Compliance Officer | For any correction that results in a change to the patient's PDGM payment group — whether an increase or a decrease — the Compliance Officer shall be notified before the correction is processed. The Compliance Officer shall assess whether: (a) the original payment was accurate, or (b) a Medicare overpayment exists that requires refund per FN-BC-004. | Before processing any payment-affecting correction; Compliance Officer notification immediately upon identification. |
| 6.4.4 | Assessing RN / Director of Nursing | Process the error correction using the EHR's OASIS correction function. The correction shall: retain the original assessment with its original responses and authentication; create a corrected version with the accurate response; document the correction date, the identity of the person making the correction, and a clinical reason notation; generate an audit trail linking the original and corrected versions per CO-DC-001. | Within 5 business days of Director of Nursing approval. |
| 6.4.5 | OASIS Transmission Coordinator | For assessments already transmitted to CMS: transmit the correction as a replacement record through the CMS-approved correction submission process per CL-CA-003. Verify CMS acceptance of the corrected record through the CMS response file. Document the correction transmission in the OASIS Submission Log per CL-CA-003. | Within 2 business days of correction processing; CMS acceptance verified within 5 business days. |
| 6.4.6 | OASIS Transmission Coordinator | For assessments not yet transmitted: the correction shall be made in the EHR and the corrected (locked) version shall be transmitted in the next regular transmission batch. Document in the OASIS Submission Log that the correction preceded transmission. | Before transmission; correction completed before transmission. |
| 6.4.7 | Director of Nursing | Document all errors identified and corrected in the OASIS Correction Log (Appendix B of this policy). The log is a cumulative record of all correction activity — reviewed monthly by the Director of Nursing for patterns, reviewed quarterly by the QAPI Committee for quality improvement implications. | At each correction; log reviewed monthly. |

#### 6.5 Inactivation Process

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Director of Nursing | Inactivation of a CMS repository record — as opposed to correction of specific item responses — is appropriate only when the entire assessment record should not have been submitted: the patient was not actually admitted; the wrong time point code was used; the assessment was submitted in error. Inactivation shall never be used to delete or conceal an assessment that should have been submitted — it is a mechanism for removing a record that has no valid place in the repository. | As clinically and administratively indicated. |
| 6.5.2 | Director of Nursing / Compliance Officer | Before initiating any inactivation, the Compliance Officer shall be notified and shall assess the billing implications of removing the record from the repository. Document the inactivation rationale and the Compliance Officer's review. | Before processing any inactivation. |
| 6.5.3 | OASIS Transmission Coordinator | Process the inactivation through the CMS-approved inactivation submission process. Verify CMS acceptance. Document in the OASIS Submission Log. | Within 5 business days of Director of Nursing / Compliance Officer approval. |

#### 6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OASIS Quality Reviewer finds systematic inaccuracy in a single assessor's work — same items wrong across multiple assessments | Director of Nursing and Compliance Officer | Assess the scope of the error pattern — how many assessments are affected, what time period, what payment impact. Initiate corrections for all identifiable errors. Targeted retraining for the assessor. Compliance Officer assesses whether the error pattern constitutes an overpayment requiring voluntary disclosure. | Scope assessment within 5 business days; corrections within 30 calendar days. |
| A correction is requested by Revenue Cycle to improve the patient's PDGM classification without clinical justification | Compliance Officer immediately notified | Reject the correction request. Compliance Officer documents the Revenue Cycle request and the rejection. Compliance Officer counsels the Revenue Cycle Director on the prohibition against financially motivated corrections. | Immediate rejection; Compliance Officer within 24 hours. |
| Agency-wide OASIS accuracy rate falls below 90% in any item category in any month | Director of Nursing and Administrator | Director of Nursing initiates agency-wide OASIS retraining within 14 calendar days. Engaging an external OASIS specialist consultant if the rate does not recover above 92% within 60 calendar days. Governing Body notification at next quarterly meeting. | Retraining within 14 calendar days; consultant within 30 days if needed. |
| Assessing RN disagrees with the OASIS Quality Reviewer's finding and escalation to Director of Nursing does not resolve the disagreement | Compliance Officer | Compliance Officer reviews the clinical record and CMS guidance independently. The Compliance Officer's determination is the agency's final coding position. If the correction is required and affects a submitted claim, initiate the correction and assess for overpayment per FN-BC-004. | Resolution within 7 calendar days. |

### 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
#### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Level 1 self-review completed before every OASIS assessment lock | EHR quality review completion log audit | ≥98% of assessments with documented self-review |
| Level 2 review completed within 5 business days for all SOC assessments | Quality Review Log audit | ≥95% reviewed within 5 business days |
| OASIS accuracy rate — GG functional items | Monthly audit | ≥95% |
| OASIS accuracy rate — wound items | Monthly audit | ≥95% |
| OASIS accuracy rate — behavioral health items | Monthly audit | ≥95% |
| OASIS accuracy rate — overall | Monthly audit | ≥95% |
| All errors identified trigger documented correction assessment | Correction Assessment Form audit | 100% — no corrections without documented clinical justification |
| Compliance Officer notified for all payment-affecting corrections | Correction file audit | 100% |
| Monthly accuracy data presented to QAPI quarterly | QAPI meeting minutes | 100% quarterly |

#### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS OASIS validation survey teams will independently assess a sample of patients and compare their clinical findings to the submitted OASIS data. They will:
Request the agency's Quality Review Program documentation — including the Quality Review Tool, Quality Review Log, Accuracy Dashboard, and corrective action records. An agency without a documented, active quality review program cannot demonstrate survey readiness.
Cross-reference OASIS responses with clinical record narrative — for every item in their sample, surveyors will verify that the clinical record contains objective documentation supporting the coded response. An OASIS response unmoored from clinical documentation is an accuracy deficiency.
Review the Correction Log — to assess whether corrections appear clinically justified or financially motivated. A pattern of corrections that consistently move PDGM payment groups upward is a red flag for upcoding.
Interview the OASIS Quality Reviewer — to verify that the person understands their role, has appropriate OASIS expertise, and can describe the quality review process.
#### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No designated OASIS Quality Reviewer — review responsibility diffused across multiple staff without dedicated expertise | No meaningful independent review; errors propagate | Designate a specific, named OASIS Quality Reviewer on the Authorized Assessor Roster; verify their advanced competency annually |
| Corrections made without documented clinical justification | False Claims Act risk; audit red flag | Correction Assessment Form required before every correction; Director of Nursing sign-off mandatory |
| Level 1 self-review treated as a checkbox without substantive review | Errors not caught before locking; pre-submission review ineffective | Include a sample of self-review checklists in the Director of Nursing's monthly audit; assess whether the checklist responses match the submitted OASIS |
| Accuracy tracking reveals low rates but no corrective action follows | Systemic accuracy deterioration; regulatory risk | Monthly Director of Nursing audit mandates individual feedback within 14 days; QAPI Performance Improvement Project trigger at 95% threshold |

10.1 All authorized RN assessors shall receive training on the OASIS quality review process within 14 calendar days of hire and annually thereafter, including: the three-level review structure; the self-review process and checklist; how to respond to Quality Reviewer findings; the error correction process; and the prohibition on financially motivated corrections.
10.2 The OASIS Quality Reviewer shall hold and maintain current advanced OASIS competency — validated through external OASIS specialist certification or equivalent rigorous assessment — and shall demonstrate current knowledge of the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual at hire and annually.

### 2. Purpose
This policy restricts OASIS completion to clinicians who have demonstrated competency through validated assessment and maintains a current authorization roster at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The OASIS instrument is the most consequential clinical document the agency produces — it drives payment, generates quality measures, and creates the clinical baseline against which all subsequent care is measured. Its completion requires not only an active California RN license and general clinical knowledge, but specific, validated competency in: the structure and logic of the OASIS data set; the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual response selection rules for each item category; the application of standardized assessment tools (BIMS, PHQ-2/PHQ-9) in validated protocols; documentation standards that substantiate every OASIS response; and the pre-submission quality review process.
An RN who is clinically excellent — an outstanding bedside nurse with years of experience — is not automatically qualified to conduct an independent OASIS assessment. The instrument has its own learning curve, its own rules, and its own pitfalls. BIMS administration is frequently performed incorrectly by assessors who were never specifically trained on the validated administration protocol. GG functional items are frequently miscoded because assessors apply intuitive clinical judgment rather than the precise CMS response selection rules. Wound staging errors — particularly reverse-staging of healing pressure injuries — occur repeatedly by clinicians who are otherwise competent wound care nurses.
This policy establishes the complete competency framework for OASIS authorization: the training program required before independent assessment; the competency validation process that gates authorization; the Authorized Assessor Roster that controls who may independently conduct assessments; the annual re-competency process that maintains authorization; and the supervisory oversight process for newly authorized assessors. It ensures that every OASIS assessment submitted by this agency was completed by someone who was specifically trained, specifically evaluated, and specifically authorized to do so.
### 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All registered nurses who are assigned or wish to be assigned to conduct comprehensive OASIS assessments
The Director of Nursing who maintains the Authorized Assessor Roster and the competency validation program
HR Director who maintains competency documentation in personnel files
IT Director who configures EHR access restrictions to OASIS assessment modules
Who may NOT independently complete OASIS assessments: Licensed Vocational Nurses (LVNs); Physical Therapists and Physical Therapist Assistants; Occupational Therapists and Certified Occupational Therapy Assistants; Speech-Language Pathologists; Medical Social Workers; Home Health Aides; any administrative or non-clinical staff. These individuals may contribute clinical data to the assessing RN during the assessment process, but they may not independently initiate, complete, or authenticate an OASIS assessment.
### 4. Policy Statement
4.1 Only registered nurses who have successfully completed the agency's OASIS Competency Program, been independently evaluated through the OASIS Competency Validation Assessment, and been listed on the current OASIS Authorized Assessor Roster by the Director of Nursing may independently conduct comprehensive OASIS assessments at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.
4.2 No RN — regardless of years of experience, prior employer's OASIS training, or OASIS certification from another organization — shall independently conduct comprehensive OASIS assessments until they have completed the agency's specific OASIS Competency Program and have been added to the Authorized Assessor Roster. Prior experience is relevant but not sufficient.
4.3 OASIS authorization is maintained through annual re-competency. An RN's authorization lapses on the anniversary of their most recent competency validation if the annual re-competency has not been completed. An assessor whose authorization has lapsed shall not independently conduct OASIS assessments until annual re-competency is completed and authorization is restored.
4.4 The OASIS Authorized Assessor Roster shall be maintained by the Director of Nursing in a format that is accessible to Medical Records staff, the OASIS Quality Reviewer, Revenue Cycle staff, and Clinical Coordinators — all of whom need to verify that a given assessor was authorized at the time of a specific assessment.
4.5 The EHR shall be configured to restrict access to the OASIS assessment module to individuals listed on the current Authorized Assessor Roster. This technical control is a backstop — it reinforces but does not replace the administrative controls established by this policy.
4.6 A newly hired RN who was an authorized OASIS assessor at a previous agency may be granted provisional authorization — allowing supervised OASIS completion alongside a current authorized assessor — for a period not to exceed 30 calendar days while completing the agency's specific OASIS Competency Program. Provisionally authorized assessors may not independently lock any OASIS assessment; every assessment initiated during the provisional period must be co-reviewed and co-authenticated by a current authorized assessor.
4.7 The OASIS Quality Reviewer role requires an additional, higher level of OASIS competency beyond general assessor authorization. The OASIS Quality Reviewer must hold advanced OASIS expertise — evidenced by external OASIS certification, completion of an advanced OASIS training program, or equivalent experience assessed and documented by the Director of Nursing. The OASIS Quality Reviewer designation is noted separately on the Authorized Assessor Roster.
### 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| OASIS Authorized Assessor | An RN who has completed the agency's OASIS Competency Program, passed the OASIS Competency Validation Assessment, and is currently listed on the OASIS Authorized Assessor Roster as authorized to independently conduct comprehensive OASIS assessments. |
| OASIS Authorized Assessor Roster | The master list, maintained by the Director of Nursing, of all currently authorized OASIS assessors at the agency — including their authorization date, most recent re-competency date, and authorization expiration date. |
| OASIS Competency Program | The structured training program that all prospective OASIS assessors must complete before authorization, as defined in Section 6.1 of this policy. |
| OASIS Competency Validation Assessment | The multi-component evaluation that gates authorization — including a written knowledge assessment, standardized tool administration demonstration, and a supervised first SOC assessment with Director of Nursing observation. |
| Provisional Authorization | A time-limited status granted to an RN with prior OASIS experience who is in the process of completing the agency's specific OASIS Competency Program. Provisional assessors may not independently lock assessments. |
| Authorization Lapse | The loss of authorized assessor status that occurs when an assessor's annual re-competency is not completed by the anniversary of their most recent competency validation. An assessor with a lapsed authorization may not independently conduct OASIS assessments until re-competency is completed. |
| OASIS Quality Reviewer | An authorized assessor with advanced OASIS expertise designated to conduct Level 2 independent reviews of completed OASIS assessments. Requires additional competency validation beyond the standard assessor program. |
| Supervised Assessment | An OASIS assessment conducted by a trainee assessor in the physical presence of a current authorized assessor, who reviews the trainee's coding decisions and co-authenticates the locked assessment during the provisional period. |

### 6. Procedures
#### 6.1 OASIS Competency Program — Initial Authorization

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Director of Nursing | Upon hire of any new RN who will be assigned OASIS assessments, enroll the RN in the OASIS Competency Program. No OASIS assessments shall be assigned to the RN until enrollment is confirmed. If the new hire has prior OASIS experience from another agency, grant provisional authorization per Section 4.6 while the program is being completed. | Within 5 business days of hire. |
| 6.1.2 | Director of Nursing / Designated OASIS Trainer | Deliver the OASIS Competency Program in the following sequence: (Module 1) Regulatory and Financial Framework: 42 CFR § 484.55; OASIS purpose; PDGM payment linkage; quality measure linkage; billing compliance implications (3 hours). (Module 2) OASIS-E2 Data Set — Structure and Time Points: assessment time point definitions, triggers, and deadlines; item applicability by time point; look-back period rules; point-in-time vs. look-back items (4 hours). (Module 3) Item-Level Coding — GG Functional Items: GG0130 (self-care), GG0170 (mobility); response option definitions; observation vs. report; activity-specific coding rules; the 6-point functional independence scale; internal consistency requirements (4 hours). (Module 4) Item-Level Coding — Wound and Skin Items: M1311–M1350 series; NPIAP staging system; reverse-staging prohibition; wound type classification; OASIS wound item navigation logic; documentation requirements (4 hours). (Module 5) Item-Level Coding — Behavioral Health Items: M1700 cognitive function; BIMS administration protocol (validated, complete); M1730 depressive feelings; PHQ-2/PHQ-9 administration (validated, complete); M1710–M1750 series (4 hours). (Module 6) Item-Level Coding — Medication, Clinical Severity, and Remaining Items: M2001–M2010 medication management items; M-series clinical severity items; MAHC-10 items; remaining applicable items (3 hours). (Module 7) Homebound Status and Skilled Need Documentation: two-part homebound criteria; patient-specific documentation standards; skilled need justification per discipline; common documentation failures (2 hours). (Module 8) Pre-Submission Quality Review: the three-level review structure; CL-OA-019 checklist process; internal consistency verification; documentation-to-OASIS alignment (2 hours). (Module 9) EHR OASIS Workflow: navigating the OASIS module in the agency's specific EHR; completing and locking assessments; mobile assessment workflow; the OASIS Completion Tracking Dashboard (2 hours). Total program: minimum 28 didactic hours; supplemented with case-based exercises for each item category. | Completed before authorization. |
| 6.1.3 | Director of Nursing / Designated Assessor | Administer the OASIS Competency Validation Assessment (Appendix A), which consists of three components: (a) Written Knowledge Assessment — 50-item multiple-choice exam covering all module content; minimum passing score: 85%; assessors who score between 80–84% may remediate and retest once; assessors who score below 80% must complete Module remediation and retake the full exam; (b) Standardized Tool Administration Demonstration — the assessor demonstrates administration of the complete BIMS (all three components in correct sequence, per validated protocol) and the PHQ-2/PHQ-9 to a simulated patient (or role-play partner); rated on a pass/fail basis by the Director of Nursing or OASIS Quality Reviewer; (c) Supervised First SOC Assessment — the assessor conducts their first OASIS assessment at a real patient's SOC in the physical presence of a current authorized assessor or the Director of Nursing, who observes the entire assessment, reviews all coding decisions, and provides real-time feedback; the supervised assessment is co-authenticated by both the trainee and the supervisor. | Completed before authorization. |
| 6.1.4 | Director of Nursing | Upon successful completion of all three components of the Competency Validation Assessment: (a) add the RN to the OASIS Authorized Assessor Roster with the authorization date; (b) notify IT Director to grant OASIS module access in the EHR; (c) file the completed Competency Validation Assessment and all scores in the RN's personnel file per HR-WM-007; (d) provide written authorization notification to the RN. | Within 5 business days of completing all three components. |

#### 6.2 Authorized Assessor Roster — Maintenance

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Director of Nursing | Maintain the OASIS Authorized Assessor Roster (Appendix B) with the following fields for each authorized assessor: full legal name; RN license number; initial authorization date; most recent annual re-competency date; authorization expiration date (12 months from most recent re-competency); current authorization status (Active / Provisional / Lapsed); OASIS Quality Reviewer designation (if applicable). | Maintained continuously; updated within 5 business days of any change. |
| 6.2.2 | Director of Nursing | Generate a monthly Roster Currency Report that identifies: assessors whose authorization will expire within the next 60 days; assessors with lapsed authorization; and any change to the Roster in the prior month. Distribute to Medical Records, OASIS Transmission Coordinator, and Revenue Cycle. | Monthly. |
| 6.2.3 | Director of Nursing | When an assessor's authorization lapses (annual re-competency not completed by the expiration date): (a) immediately update the Roster status to "Lapsed"; (b) notify IT Director to suspend OASIS module access; (c) notify Clinical Coordinator that the assessor is not available for OASIS assessment assignments; (d) initiate contact with the assessor to schedule immediate re-competency. No OASIS assessment conducted by an assessor with lapsed authorization after the expiration date is valid — each such assessment must be reviewed and, if necessary, re-conducted by an authorized assessor. | On the expiration date if re-competency is not completed. |
| 6.2.4 | IT Director | Configure and maintain EHR access controls that restrict OASIS assessment module access to the individuals currently listed as Active or Provisional on the Authorized Assessor Roster. Update access within 5 business days of any Roster change. | Within 5 business days of any Roster change. |

#### 6.3 Annual Re-Competency — Authorization Maintenance

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Director of Nursing | Generate an annual re-competency alert 60 days before each assessor's authorization expiration date. Notify the assessor and schedule the re-competency process. | 60 days before expiration. |
| 6.3.2 | Director of Nursing | Conduct annual re-competency for every authorized assessor before their authorization expiration date. Annual re-competency consists of: (a) OASIS Updates Review: review of any changes to the OASIS data set, CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual, or assessment time point requirements issued since the prior re-competency (minimum 1 hour if changes are present; 30 minutes if no changes); (b) Accuracy Feedback Review: structured review with the Director of Nursing of the assessor's OASIS accuracy audit results from the prior 12 months — specific items with errors, correct responses, CMS guidance citations; (c) Annual Written Assessment: abbreviated 25-item written assessment focusing on items where the assessor had identified errors in the prior year and any new or revised CMS guidance; minimum passing score 85%; (d) Standardized Tool Re-Demonstration: if the assessor had a documented BIMS or PHQ-2/PHQ-9 administration error in the prior year, re-demonstration is required; if no prior error, annual BIMS re-demonstration is still required to maintain proficiency. | Before authorization expiration; completed re-competency updates the expiration date. |
| 6.3.3 | Director of Nursing | Document the annual re-competency completion and all scores in the assessor's personnel file. Update the Authorized Assessor Roster with the new re-competency date and new authorization expiration date. Notify IT Director to update EHR access as applicable. | Within 5 business days of re-competency completion. |

#### 6.4 Provisional Authorization — Management

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Director of Nursing | When granting provisional authorization to a new hire with prior OASIS experience: (a) document the provisional authorization with its start and expiration date (30 calendar days maximum); (b) add the assessor to the Roster with "Provisional" status; (c) notify IT Director to grant limited OASIS access (view only, or access with mandatory co-authentication requirement); (d) assign a current authorized assessor as the provisional assessor's supervisor for all OASIS assessments during the provisional period; (e) clearly communicate to the provisional assessor that they may not independently lock any assessment during the provisional period. | Within 5 business days of hire. |
| 6.4.2 | Supervising Authorized Assessor | Review and co-authenticate every OASIS assessment initiated by the provisional assessor. Document the supervisory review — including any coding decisions discussed and corrected — in the OASIS Quality Review Log. | For every assessment during the provisional period. |
| 6.4.3 | Director of Nursing | Upon completion of the OASIS Competency Program and Competency Validation Assessment, convert the provisional assessor to Active authorization. If the provisional period expires (30 days) before the program is completed, remove the provisional authorization until completion. | Upon competency validation completion; immediately upon provisional period expiration without completion. |

#### 6.5 OASIS Quality Reviewer — Advanced Authorization

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.5.1 | Director of Nursing | Designate a specific authorized assessor for the OASIS Quality Reviewer role. The designee must demonstrate advanced OASIS expertise through one of the following: (a) external OASIS certification from a recognized national organization; (b) completion of an accredited advanced OASIS training program of minimum 20 hours in addition to the standard Competency Program; (c) documented prior experience as an OASIS quality reviewer with demonstrated competency at a prior agency, assessed through a Director of Nursing competency interview and case review exercise. | At the time of initial designation; maintained and re-evaluated annually. |
| 6.5.2 | Director of Nursing | Note the OASIS Quality Reviewer designation on the Authorized Assessor Roster. Maintain documentation of the advanced competency basis for the designation in the Quality Reviewer's personnel file. | At designation; maintained. |
| 6.5.3 | Director of Nursing | Ensure that at least one OASIS Quality Reviewer is designated and active at all times. If the designated Quality Reviewer is unavailable (leave, separation), the Director of Nursing shall serve as the Quality Reviewer until a replacement is designated and qualified. | Continuously. |

#### 6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| An OASIS assessment is discovered to have been completed by a non-authorized individual (LVN, therapist, unauthorized RN) | Director of Nursing and Compliance Officer | OASIS must be reviewed and if necessary re-completed by an authorized assessor. Assess billing implications with Revenue Cycle. Document all corrective actions. Provide corrective counseling to the individual who completed the unauthorized assessment. | Review within 5 business days; billing assessment within 10 business days. |
| An authorized assessor has repeated competency failures at annual re-competency | Director of Nursing | After a second failed written assessment attempt, the Director of Nursing shall revoke authorization pending completion of targeted remediation. The assessor shall not conduct OASIS assessments during the remediation period. If re-competency cannot be achieved within 30 calendar days of revocation, assess employment implications with HR. | Authorization revoked within 24 hours of second failure; remediation within 30 calendar days. |
| The agency has only one authorized assessor and that assessor is unexpectedly unavailable | Administrator and Director of Nursing | The Director of Nursing shall temporarily conduct OASIS assessments (if they are an authorized assessor) or shall immediately initiate provisional authorization for an RN with prior experience. Contact Healthcare Coalition or a temporary staffing agency if needed to ensure assessment coverage. | Interim coverage within 24 hours. |

### 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
#### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All OASIS assessments conducted by authorized assessors | Cross-reference submitted assessments with Authorized Assessor Roster | 100% — zero assessments by unauthorized individuals |
| Authorized Assessor Roster current and complete | Roster audit | 100% — updated within 5 business days of every change |
| Annual re-competency completed before expiration for all assessors | Roster expiration date audit | 100% — no lapsed authorizations at any time |
| OASIS Competency Validation Assessment completed before initial authorization | Personnel file audit | 100% |
| OASIS Quality Reviewer advanced competency documented | Personnel file audit | 100% — at designation and annually |
| EHR OASIS access restricted to current Roster | EHR access audit | 100% consistent with current Roster |

#### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
CMS surveyors will request the agency's OASIS Authorized Assessor Roster and will cross-reference it against the assessors who completed submitted OASIS assessments during the survey look-back period. They will request personnel files for assessors and verify that competency validation documentation is present. They will ask the Director of Nursing to describe the authorization process. An OASIS assessment completed by a non-RN or by an unauthorized RN is a Condition-level deficiency.
#### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RN hired with "OASIS experience" and immediately begins independent assessments without agency-specific competency program | Unauthorized assessment; accuracy risk; potential Condition-level deficiency | Zero-exception policy: no independent OASIS completion before agency Competency Program completion; provisional authorization with supervised assessments during transition |
| Annual re-competency treated as a brief policy sign-off without substantive competency re-evaluation | Authorization maintained by paperwork rather than actual competency | Annual re-competency includes written assessment, accuracy feedback, and tool re-demonstration; Director of Nursing conducts all re-competency in person |
| EHR access not updated after assessor's authorization lapses | Lapsed assessor can still access and complete OASIS in EHR | EHR access update triggered by Roster change within 5 business days; IT Director monthly access audit against current Roster |
| OASIS Quality Reviewer designation not supported by advanced competency documentation | Quality Reviewer cannot effectively identify errors in complex items | Advanced competency documentation required at designation; external certification strongly preferred |

## CL-OA-004 — OASIS Item-Level Guidance Compliance
### 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | CL-OA-004 |
| Policy Title | OASIS Item-Level Guidance Compliance |
| Domain | CL — Clinical Operations |
| Subdomain | OA — OASIS & Assessment Governance |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Director of Nursing |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |

### 2. Purpose
This policy requires all OASIS responses to align with the current CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual and prohibits agency-created coding interpretations that conflict with CMS guidance at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The OASIS Guidance Manual is the definitive authority for every coding decision — not the assessor's clinical intuition, not the agency's internally developed "cheat sheets," not the guidance from a prior version of OASIS, not the interpretation provided by a revenue cycle vendor, and not what the agency believes CMS "should" mean by a particular item definition.
The history of home health compliance enforcement is littered with agencies that developed their own internal OASIS coding conventions — often driven by payment optimization concerns — that deviated from or directly contradicted the CMS Guidance Manual. These deviations, when identified through OASIS validation surveys, MAC audits, or OIG investigations, produced findings of systematic upcoding or inaccurate data reporting that led to recoupments, corrective action plans, and in some cases False Claims Act settlements. The agency that codes the GG functional items by asking the patient what they can do, rather than by observing what they actually do during the visit, is not just making a clinical error — it is systematically overstating functional impairment in a way that increases PDGM payment. The agency that codes wound stages without applying the NPIAP staging system is not just making an assessment error — it is generating invalid quality measure data that misrepresents the agency's patient outcomes.
This policy establishes the absolute authority of the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual, the process for accessing and maintaining current guidance, the prohibition on agency-created alternative interpretations, the process for resolving item-level ambiguity through legitimate channels, and the governance of guidance updates when CMS revises the OASIS instrument or the Guidance Manual.
### 3. Scope
This policy applies to:
All authorized OASIS assessors who make item-level coding decisions
The Director of Nursing who oversees coding guidance compliance
The OASIS Quality Reviewer who validates item-level coding against the Guidance Manual
The Compliance Officer who oversees the prohibition on financially motivated coding deviations
Any educational materials, training programs, reference tools, or coding aids used by the agency in connection with OASIS assessment
### 4. Policy Statement
4.1 The CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual — the most current version, as published by CMS — is the sole authoritative source for all OASIS item-level coding decisions at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. No other source has equivalent authority.
4.2 When an assessor has a question about the correct coding of any OASIS item for a specific patient situation, the correct process is: first, consult the current CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual for the specific item; second, review the item-specific FAQ or Q&A materials published by CMS or the relevant state OASIS contractor; third, consult the Director of Nursing or OASIS Quality Reviewer for clinical adjudication; fourth, if the guidance remains unclear, submit the question to the CMS OASIS contractor or the state OASIS coordinator through the official Q&A submission process. At no point in this process shall the assessor create an agency-specific interpretation that is not grounded in and consistent with CMS guidance.
4.3 The agency shall maintain a current, accessible copy of the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual in the EHR reference library and shall update it within 30 calendar days of any CMS revision to the Guidance Manual. Assessors shall access the Guidance Manual from the agency's EHR reference library — not from memory, from prior-version documents, or from third-party materials that have not been verified for consistency with the current Guidance Manual.
4.4 The following practices are explicitly prohibited at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.:
(a) Using a prior version of the OASIS Guidance Manual as the basis for any coding decision after a new version has been published and adopted.
(b) Applying an internally developed "cheat sheet," "quick reference guide," or coding shortcut that selects OASIS response options through a decision pathway not grounded in the current CMS Guidance Manual. All quick reference materials used in OASIS coding must be verified against the current Guidance Manual and must explicitly note that they are supplements to — not replacements of — the Guidance Manual.
(c) Coding OASIS items in a systematic manner that departs from the Guidance Manual's response selection rules — including but not limited to: coding GG functional items based solely on patient or caregiver report without observing the patient perform the activity; coding wound items without undressing dressings and directly observing wounds; coding behavioral health items without administering the required standardized tools in validated protocols; or reverse-staging healing pressure injuries.
(d) Accepting OASIS coding instructions from revenue cycle staff, billing consultants, or management personnel that deviate from the CMS Guidance Manual's response selection rules, for any reason — including payment optimization.
(e) Retaining in the agency's reference library any OASIS coding guidance, training material, or reference tool that conflicts with the current version of the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual, without clearly marking the conflicting material as "SUPERSEDED — DO NOT USE."
4.5 When the CMS Guidance Manual provides an unclear or ambiguous response to a specific clinical scenario — a situation that genuinely exists for some items — the assessor shall use the clinical reasoning documentation process per CL-OA-012 to document the specific ambiguity, the interpretive approach applied, and the clinical basis for the selected response. This documentation does not authorize deviation from CMS guidance — it documents the assessor's good-faith application of judgment where the guidance itself is ambiguous.
4.6 The agency shall track CMS OASIS guidance updates through the CMS website, CMS OASIS listservs, and state OASIS contractor communications, and shall disseminate updates to all authorized assessors within 14 calendar days of any change to the Guidance Manual.
### 5. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual | The current, definitive, CMS-published document providing item-specific guidance for all OASIS data collection decisions, including definitions of response options, look-back periods, time points at which items are collected, and special circumstances. The authoritative source for all coding decisions. |
| Item-Level Guidance | The specific instructions, definitions, response option descriptions, special circumstances guidance, and coding rules provided in the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual for a specific OASIS item. |
| Agency-Created Coding Interpretation | Any OASIS coding rule, convention, shortcut, or guidance document developed by the agency, its management, its revenue cycle team, or any third party that is not grounded in or consistent with the current CMS Guidance Manual. Prohibited by this policy. |
| Guidance Ambiguity | A situation where the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual does not clearly and unambiguously resolve the correct coding response for a specific clinical scenario. Requires clinical reasoning documentation per CL-OA-012. |
| CMS OASIS Guidance Update | A revision to the OASIS data set, the OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual, the OASIS Q&A database, or associated CMS guidance documents that changes item definitions, response options, collection rules, or coding instructions. |
| Quick Reference Material | Any abbreviated coding guide, summary document, or reference card used by assessors to support OASIS completion — permissible only if grounded in and consistent with the current CMS Guidance Manual and clearly labeled as a supplement to the Guidance Manual. |
| OASIS Contractor | The CMS-contracted organization responsible for providing training, technical assistance, and Q&A resolution for OASIS-related questions. The official channel for submitting questions about OASIS coding not resolved by the Guidance Manual itself. |

### 6. Procedures
#### 6.1 Access to Current CMS OASIS Guidance

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.1.1 | Director of Nursing | Maintain a current copy of the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual in the agency's EHR reference library, accessible to all authorized assessors at any time from any device with EHR access. The EHR reference library copy shall be the current version — when CMS publishes a new version, the outdated version shall be replaced within 30 calendar days and marked "SUPERSEDED" if retained for reference. | Current version maintained continuously; update within 30 calendar days of CMS publication. |
| 6.1.2 | Director of Nursing | Subscribe to the CMS OASIS listserv, state OASIS contractor notifications, and relevant CMS email updates to receive notification of Guidance Manual revisions, Q&A updates, and coding clarifications as soon as they are issued. | Subscriptions maintained continuously. |
| 6.1.3 | Director of Nursing | When a CMS OASIS Guidance update is received, assess its impact: (a) identify which items have been changed; (b) identify how the changes affect current assessor practice; (c) determine whether immediate correction of any in-progress assessments is needed; (d) prepare a training update for all authorized assessors. | Within 5 business days of receiving the update. |
| 6.1.4 | Director of Nursing | Distribute the guidance update to all authorized assessors within 14 calendar days, with a written summary of: what changed; how it differs from the prior guidance; practical examples illustrating the new coding approach; and any assessments submitted under the prior guidance that may require correction. Obtain written acknowledgment from each assessor that they received and reviewed the update. | Within 14 calendar days of the update. |

#### 6.2 Item-Level Ambiguity Resolution

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.2.1 | Assessing RN | When encountering a clinical situation where the correct OASIS coding is unclear — because the patient's presentation does not map cleanly to the Guidance Manual's response option definitions — follow this sequential resolution process: Step 1: Review the complete item-specific guidance in the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual, including special circumstances, Q&A sections, and any relevant examples provided. Step 2: Search the CMS OASIS Q&A database (available on the CMS website) for existing Q&As addressing the specific scenario. Step 3: Consult the Director of Nursing or OASIS Quality Reviewer for clinical adjudication. Step 4: If the ambiguity cannot be resolved through Steps 1–3, the Director of Nursing may submit a formal question to the state OASIS contractor for official guidance. | Before finalizing the coding decision. |
| 6.2.2 | Assessing RN | Document the ambiguity resolution process per CL-OA-012: note the specific ambiguity, the steps taken to resolve it, the clinical reasoning applied, and the final coding decision with its basis. This documentation is both a clinical record entry and a compliance defense if the coding decision is later questioned. | In the assessment narrative; within 24 hours of the decision. |
| 6.2.3 | Director of Nursing | Compile a log of recurring item-level ambiguities encountered by the agency's assessors. Use the log to: identify training needs; prepare pre-emptive guidance for common ambiguous scenarios; and submit formal questions to the OASIS contractor to obtain official resolution. Share the log and any official Q&A responses with all authorized assessors. | Log reviewed quarterly; formal Q&A submissions as warranted. |

#### 6.3 Audit of Coding Materials for Guidance Compliance

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.3.1 | Director of Nursing | Conduct an annual audit of all OASIS coding materials in the agency's possession — including printed reference guides, digital reference cards, training slides, coding worksheets, and any third-party training materials — to verify that each material is: (a) consistent with the current version of the CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual; (b) clearly labeled as a supplement to — not replacement of — the Guidance Manual; (c) dated and identified as applicable to the current OASIS version. | Annually; concurrent with the annual OASIS re-competency cycle. |
| 6.3.2 | Director of Nursing | Remove or destroy any coding material that: contains instructions or response-selection shortcuts that are inconsistent with the current Guidance Manual; was prepared for a prior version of the OASIS without having been updated for the current version; or contains language suggesting that payment optimization should influence coding decisions. Document the removal and the reason in the materials audit log. | Immediately upon identification. |
| 6.3.3 | Compliance Officer | Conduct a quarterly review of the Director of Nursing's OASIS coding materials audit log and assess whether any identified deviations suggest systemic compliance risk requiring investigation or corrective action. | Quarterly. |

#### 6.4 Governance of Third-Party OASIS Training and Reference Materials

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6.4.1 | Director of Nursing | Before distributing any third-party OASIS training material — including materials from training vendors, professional associations, or peer agencies — verify its consistency with the current CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual. If any third-party material conflicts with the Guidance Manual, the Guidance Manual governs. Annotate any conflicting third-party material with the correct guidance before distribution. | Before any distribution. |
| 6.4.2 | Director of Nursing | Assess all agency EHR-embedded OASIS coding guidance or drop-down prompts for consistency with the current CMS Guidance Manual annually and whenever the OASIS instrument is updated. Report any EHR-embedded guidance that is inconsistent with current CMS guidance to the IT Director and EHR vendor for correction. | Annually; within 30 calendar days of any OASIS update. |
| 6.4.3 | Director of Nursing | Do not accept OASIS coding instruction from revenue cycle consultants, coding vendors, or billing companies that selects response options on the basis of payment optimization rather than clinical accuracy. Report any such instruction to the Compliance Officer immediately. | Immediately upon identification. |

#### 6.5 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| An assessor is found to be using an outdated version of the Guidance Manual | Director of Nursing | Immediately provide the current Guidance Manual. Assess all assessments completed under the outdated guidance for potential coding errors. Initiate corrections for any identified errors per CL-OA-002. | Immediate guidance correction; assessment review within 14 calendar days. |
| Revenue cycle staff or management instructs assessors to code in a specific way to increase PDGM payment | Compliance Officer | The Compliance Officer initiates a compliance investigation per CO-CP-007. Immediate corrective communication to all parties. Assessment of all assessments coded under the instruction for potential corrections and overpayment. Governing Body notification. | Immediate Compliance Officer involvement; investigation within 24 hours. |
| A CMS OASIS Guidance update contradicts a prior training that assessors received | Director of Nursing | Issue an immediate update communication to all assessors. Schedule a focused training session on the changed item within 14 calendar days. Review recent assessments for items affected by the change. Initiate corrections per CL-OA-002 for assessments coded under the superseded guidance if the change affects clinical accuracy of submitted data. | Immediate communication; training within 14 calendar days; assessment review within 30 calendar days. |
| An assessor consistently selects the highest severity response option for GG functional items without documenting observation of the patient performing the activity | Director of Nursing and Compliance Officer | Director of Nursing conducts targeted retraining on GG observation requirement. OASIS Quality Reviewer conducts a 100% review of the assessor's GG items from the past 90 days. Compliance Officer assesses whether the pattern constitutes systematic upcoding. | Retraining within 7 calendar days; comprehensive review within 30 calendar days. |

### 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations
#### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual accessible in EHR reference library | IT / Medical Records audit | 100% — current version confirmed at each quarterly review |
| All guidance updates distributed to assessors within 14 calendar days | Distribution log with dates | 100% |
| No coding materials in use that conflict with current Guidance Manual | Annual materials audit | 100% — no non-conforming materials in active use |
| Item-level ambiguity documentation present for all complex coding decisions | Monthly OASIS quality review per CL-OA-002 | ≥95% of audited ambiguous items with documented reasoning |
| No revenue-motivated coding instruction identified | Compliance Officer quarterly review | Zero violations |

#### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For
Surveyors will select specific OASIS items from a patient sample and will bring the current CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual to compare the agency's coding decisions against. They will verify that the assessor can articulate the CMS guidance basis for the selected response. They will also review the agency's coding reference materials and assess whether any of these materials contain response-selection shortcuts that bypass or misrepresent the Guidance Manual's rules.
#### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Assessors coding from memory without consulting the Guidance Manual | Inaccurate responses based on clinical intuition rather than CMS rules | EHR reference library Guidance Manual accessible at every visit via mobile; training emphasizes "when in doubt, look it up" |
| Agency-developed quick reference guides that simplify response selection in ways that deviate from the Guidance Manual | Systematic coding inaccuracy; potential upcoding | Annual materials audit; all quick reference materials must cite specific Guidance Manual page references |
| Guidance Manual update not distributed — assessors still coding under prior version | Coding errors for changed items | CMS subscription; Director of Nursing update protocol within 14 calendar days |
| Revenue cycle pressure on assessors to code toward higher payment groups | False Claims Act exposure | Zero-tolerance policy in this policy statement; Compliance hotline for reporting; Compliance Officer quarterly review |

### 10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements
10.1 All authorized assessors shall receive training on Guidance Manual compliance requirements within their initial OASIS Competency Program and annually at re-competency, including: accessing the current Guidance Manual in the EHR reference library; the prohibition on agency-created coding interpretations; the ambiguity resolution process; and the prohibition on revenue-motivated coding.
10.2 When CMS issues a Guidance Manual update, all authorized assessors shall complete an update training session and sign a receipt acknowledgment before coding items affected by the update.
10.3 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix A) within 14 calendar days of the effective date, any revision, or hire/appointment.

Maintained per EN-LC-001. Substantive revisions require Governing Body approval. Non-substantive revisions approved by Administrator.
